submitter: bug_122_ink_target_and_switch — ROUND 2, resubmitted on trail d60aab29 after REVISE
rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 returned REVISE and it found a real defect, so this is a revision, not a defence. Verdict health checked before acting on it (12 reviewers, 5 relevance-gated abstentions, unreadable 0, gated_by_truncation false), because this lane's own record is that an earlier seat's reviews came back two-thirds truncated and an approval from seats that failed to render looks identical from outside.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE CODE — one defect, found independently by bug_historian and guardian, and they were right.

`inkPolicy{}` is Go's free zero value and it is the DANGEROUS state: enabled=false, minRatio=0, i.e. 'silently emit nothing'. On a shared builder that is indistinguishable from a deliberate kill and raises no error anywhere. Every caller is wired today — it is a signature change, so the compiler catches a miss — but a FUTURE call site that forgets to thread a policy would quietly restore pre-repair behaviour on everything it renders. That is 016b §9 item 7 / bugs_open/093: the generic mechanism patched at one call site.

Fixed with an explicit `resolved` flag set only by the two sanctioned constructors. An unresolved policy is treated as a caller bug: fail SAFE (use the shipped default, still emit) and log at Error so it cannot hide. Shape taken from ChromeLinkPolicy/LoadChromeLinkPolicy, which the reuse seat named as this package's existing per-site policy convention — the discipline worth copying is that it resolves toward the safe direction on every failure path, which is exactly what my zero value violated. Mutations M6 (delete the guard) and M7 (keep the repair, drop the log) each fail the new test.

Also fixed, from editquality's 'missing': platform/colour/legible_variant_test.go still recorded the declined-5.0 argument as live guidance. I had quoted and answered it in the new file and never touched the original — a decision overruled in one file and left current in another, which is precisely the failure mode that let the ink==text belief survive six days. Marked OVERRULED in place, argument preserved, now pointing at the production pin.

THE REST ARE ANSWERED WITH MEASUREMENTS RATHER THAN ARGUMENT. Each seat asked a question whose answer could have gone the other way; none did, and the checks are recorded so nobody re-runs them.

debug_historian (HIGH) was the one that mattered most and it was right to ask: status='deferred' alone does NOT make a work item undispatchable — only the PAIR with an empty handler_agent does. Measured: 829a8f3e's handler_agent IS empty and claimed_by IS NULL. That pair is not my invention; discovery_checks/remit.go:29-41 already documents it as 'why the residue item cannot be dispatched, twice over'. Both claim predicates filter status IN ('triaged','approved') (claim_work_item_action.go:102, load_work_item_actions.go:651); the only promoter I can find touches status='detected' only (triage_detect_items_action.go); and remit.go records that stale-work-item-reaper touches status='triaged' AND pipeline='build'. So the park holds on the documented contract, not on my say-so.

editquality (medium) asked whether spec.Defaults could make these keys dead. No ActionInputSpec is registered for render_css_from_spec at all — so there are no Defaults to shadow anything — and resolveInkPolicy reads `config` directly rather than through ExtractActionInputs, which builds its own Values map. Positive evidence rather than an absence argument: this same function already reads theme_name and theme_id from the same map with the same helper family, and those demonstrably work.

A check I did not think to run, and which could have been a genuine defect in the kill-switch: the emit-nothing path is only safe if every consumer carries a var() fallback. Measured across all four surfaces — content_components, site_components, layouts, page_components — 46 rows reference an ink var and ZERO are bare. A control was run before believing the zero: the regex matches `var(--color-primary-ink)` and does not match the two-level form. Nothing in the platform enforces that invariant, so it is now recorded at the field with its re-check query.

reuse_agent (medium) named sites.style_overrides as a purpose-built home. Checked: the column exists, 0 of 40 sites populate it, and NO Go code reads it. Putting the switch there means also building its reader, and the result would be a mechanism whose only consumer is itself — the dead-config shape this seam already exists to avoid. I have stated this rather than assumed it, and I would accept being overruled: a dead column built for this purpose is arguably a reason to wire it up, not to route around it. That is a judgement, not a measurement.

architecture (low) asked for the optional-key count against RFC_022's N=10. The budget applies to SHARED actions (>=2 live carriers); render_css_from_spec has exactly 1 (webdesign-agent). Separately and more importantly: the audit script does not list this action AT ALL, because it sources declarations from RegisterActionInputSpec and none is registered — so its silence is the gate not looking, not a pass, and it is not cited as one.

plan.summary: Raise the ink contrast target to 5.0 per owner ruling; split the AA floor into its own constant so the ruling does not leak into the filled-control mechanism; add a default-ON per-site kill-switch with a clamped contrast override, so rollback is a config edit rather than a revert + rebuild + roll.

edits.rationale: inkMinContrast 4.5 -> 5.0. The comment quotes the argument AGAINST 5.0 that this lane already recorded and declined it on -- a cushion 'buys absorption without fixing a wrong ground and would imply cover for grounds nobody models' -- because that argument is good and must not be lost by being overruled. It is answered rather than ignored: the four-ground compositing is untouched, so the cushion is not substituting for ground modelling. The owner's counter is empirical -- this lane has twice discovered a ground it was not measuring, and the 0.05 section overlay cost 0.62 of ratio against a first-hit headroom of 0.02-0.09.

Split inkFloorContrast (4.5, the WCAG AA floor) out as a separate constant and repoint pickInkOn at it. THIS IS THE SCOPE-CONTROL EDIT. pickInkOn serves the --color-<x>-TEXT slots (ink on a filled control); the ruling was about --color-<x>-INK (links and eyebrows on the page ground). Sharing one constant meant a ruling about links would silently retune every button label in the fleet. inkCeilingContrast (7.0, AAA) added as the upper clamp: above it, the lightness search walks to near-white or near-black on most palettes, which is the de-branding this entire repair exists to stop.

Add inkPolicy{enabled, minRatio} + defaultInkPolicy() + resolveInkPolicy(config, siteID, logger), and thread the policy through buildLegibleInkDefaults. The disabled path emits NOTHING rather than an empty block -- that is the whole contract, because every consumer opts in with var(--color-primary-ink, var(--color-primary)), so an absent companion falls through to the palette colour and reaches the exact pre-2026-08-06 behaviour with no revert, rebuild or roll. Reuses the pre-existing toStringSlice and configFloatField helpers; the first version of this edit shipped its own copies and the compiler caught the collision, which is the librarian seat's prior-art objection arriving a second time in one week.

Resolve the policy at the call site from the step config and the already-resolved siteID, and pass it in. Resolved here rather than inside the builder so the builder stays a pure function of (css, palette, policy) and the pinned tests can drive it at an explicit target. siteID may be empty -- the render path resolves it from collectedData and it is not guaranteed -- and an empty siteID cannot match the disable list, which is the safe direction: the fix stays on.
edits.sketch:
inkPol := resolveInkPolicy(config, siteID, logger)
inkDefaults := buildLegibleInkDefaults(renderedCSS, mergedPalette, inkPol, logger)

edits.rationale: Pins production emission AT THE LIVE THRESHOLD, in this package, because the existing pin in platform/colour is at the fixed colour.AANormal constant (4.5) and went stale-but-green the instant the target moved -- it now describes seven colours that no longer ship. A pin whose threshold cannot follow production is a pin on a hypothetical. All seven expected values were computed by a SEPARATE implementation of the HSL/WCAG maths BEFORE this file was written, from palettes transcribed off the served stylesheets this session; that implementation reproduces all seven existing 4.5 pins exactly, which is what earns its 5.0 column any trust. Also includes TestInkPolicy_MinRatioActuallyReachesTheDerivation, which exists because defaultInkPolicy().minRatio == inkMinContrast, so a builder that ignored the policy entirely and read the package constant would satisfy every other test in the file.

ROUND 2 FIX for the round-1 defect. Add inkPolicy.resolved, set only by defaultInkPolicy and resolveInkPolicy. buildLegibleInkDefaults treats an unresolved policy as a caller bug: falls back to the shipped default (fails SAFE, still emits) and logs at Error (cannot hide). Without this, a bare inkPolicy{} silently emits nothing, which is pre-repair behaviour with no error - the failure both bug_historian and guardian named. Also documents at the `enabled` field the measured invariant the disabled path depends on (46 ink references, 0 bare) with its re-check query, because nothing enforces it.

ROUND 2, from editquality's 'missing'. The comment recording the declined-5.0 decision was left live in its original location while being quoted-and-answered elsewhere, so a future session reading this file first inherits overruled guidance as current. Marked OVERRULED in place with the date and the ruling, argument preserved (it was answered, not dismissed), and pointed at the production pin. Also states plainly that this test pins the ALGORITHM at the fixed AANormal constant and therefore stayed green while its seven hexes stopped shipping.

ROUND 2. TestInkPolicy_UnresolvedZeroValueFailsSafeAndLoud pins the new guard's full contract: a bare inkPolicy{} must still EMIT (fail safe), must emit the SHIPPED default value, and must log at Error (fail loud). Carries a control asserting that a resolved+disabled policy still emits nothing, so the guard cannot pass by having quietly broken the kill-switch. Mutation-proved: M6 deletes the guard, M7 keeps the repair but drops the log; each fails this test alone.

grounded_in: [owner, in chat, 2026-08-14] "Decision 2: 5.0, Decision 3: yes a switch." — The whole authority for this change. Given after being shown that the shipped emissions sat 0.01-0.14 above the AA line, and after being shown the per-site blast radius.

[platform/colour/legible_variant_test.go, TestLegibleVariant_EmittedHexIsPinnedForRealPalettes] "A reviewer proposed walking to 5.0 for absorption; that was declined because it buys a cushion without fixing a wrong ground and would imply cover for grounds nobody models." — The recorded argument this ruling overturns. Quoted at the constant rather than deleted, and answered: the four-ground compositing is untouched, so the cushion is additive to ground modelling, not a substitute for it.

[council verdict afcec886-f84c-4fb4-8876-43502e70965b, guardian seat, medium x2] "changes a shared function's output for 14 of 18 sites with no canary gate and no kill-switch; rollback is revert + rebuild + roll + re-render, not a config flip" — The switch answers this objection directly, in the seat's own terms. The lane declined it at the time with a sound reason (a default-OFF flag leaves the broken derivation as the default) -- which is why this is an OPT-OUT, preserving that reason while satisfying the objection.

[CLAUDE.md, OWNER RULING 2026-07-29 section 2] "The only mechanism that actually holds a seam back is a default-OFF switch, and the owner has ruled we will NOT require one (its cost is a mechanism rotting unexercised)." — Why the switch defaults ON. This is not the 2026-08-02 opt-in-default-OFF shape and should not be reviewed as one: it adds no new authority, it makes existing authority revocable.

[measured this session, served stylesheets, bare curl 200 on all seven domains] "dartsonline primary-ink at 4.5 = #8a97bd (4.598); at 5.0 = #94a0c2 (5.122). All 7 sites find a variant at 5.0; none falls through to the palette walk." — Establishes the ruling is implementable everywhere it applies -- no site is pushed off the lightness search into a substitution, which would have reintroduced the original de-branding defect at a higher target.

[measured this session, live DB, all five CSS surfaces] "9 templates opt into the ink vars: 4 content_components and 5 layouts. The 5 layouts carry `a { color: var(--color-accent-ink, var(--color-accent)) }` -- every in-prose link. dartsonline's served stylesheet contains ZERO live references to either ink var." — Scope evidence, and it corrected a figure already given to the owner. It also means the canary site exercises the change far less than the sites that follow it -- which is why the owner added webdesign.co.uk as a second canary.

[measured 2026-08-14, live DB] site_work_items 829a8f3e: status='deferred', handler_agent EMPTY, claimed_by NULL. discovery_checks/remit.go:29-41 documents that exact pair as undispatchable 'twice over'; claim_work_item_action.go:102 and load_work_item_actions.go:651 both filter status IN ('triaged','approved'). — Answers debug_historian's HIGH objection with the codebase's own contract rather than my assertion.

[measured 2026-08-14, all four CSS surfaces] 46 rows reference --color-primary-ink or --color-accent-ink; 0 are bare (no var() fallback). Control: the regex matches 'var(--color-primary-ink)' and does NOT match 'var(--color-primary-ink, var(--color-primary))'. — The kill-switch's emit-nothing path is only safe because of this, and nothing enforces it, so it is now recorded at the field with its re-check query.

[measured 2026-08-14] No RegisterActionInputSpec exists for render_css_from_spec, so no spec.Defaults can shadow the new config keys; and resolveInkPolicy reads params.StepConfig.Config directly, the same map from which this function already reads theme_name/theme_id. — Answers editquality's dead-config-key objection.

[measured 2026-08-14] sites.style_overrides: 0 of 40 sites populated, and zero Go readers outside tests. render_css_from_spec has 1 live carrier, so RFC_022's N=10 (>=2 carriers) does not apply — and scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh does not list the action at all, because it sources declarations from RegisterActionInputSpec. Its silence is the gate not looking, not a pass.
plan.risks:
THE ONE I MOST WANT CHECKED: the inkFloorContrast split changes pickInkOn's behaviour relative to a world where the constant had simply been raised -- i.e. it is a decision about how far the ruling reaches, made by me rather than by the owner. I read 'links and small labels' as not covering button labels on filled controls. If a seat reads the ruling as fleet-wide, the split is wrong and pickInkOn should move to 5.0 too. Measured: pickInkOn is reached by the --color-<x>-text slots, which 0 of 18 layouts declared as of the 08-06 measurement in this file's own comment, so the practical blast radius of getting this wrong is small either way -- but the direction is a judgement, not a measurement.

The per-site kill-switch keys on site UUID, not domain. An operator reaching for it during an incident has a domain in hand and must look the UUID up. Domain was not used because the render action resolves siteID from collectedData and does not carry the domain; adding a lookup puts a DB query in the render path. Mitigated by whitespace/case tolerance and by the disable being logged at Warn with the site_id echoed, but it is friction at exactly the wrong moment.

resolveInkPolicy silently ignores a mistyped legible_ink_enabled (e.g. the string "false" rather than the boolean). Deliberate -- an unparseable config must not fail the render, because a stylesheet that does not render is worse than one rendered at the default -- and pinned by a test. But it means a typo in an incident config edit leaves the fix ON while the operator believes it is off. The Warn line is the only signal. An alternative is to fail loudly on a present-but-mistyped key; I did not take it and would accept being overruled.

This change is live-on-commit in the sense that matters: the next fleet roll ships it, and any re-render of any of the 14 affected sites then picks it up. The dartsonline re-render that was already dispatched at 4.5 has been HELD (site_work_items 829a8f3e, triaged -> deferred, guarded on status) precisely so the owner's visual gate lands on 5.0 values rather than 4.5 ones. If that hold is lifted before this rolls, the canary shows the wrong colours and the gate is spent on them.

ROUND 2 ADDITIONS.

The `resolved` flag makes the zero value safe but does not make it IMPOSSIBLE — Go will still hand any caller a bare inkPolicy{}, and the guard catches it at runtime rather than at compile time. A stronger version would make the struct unconstructable outside its constructors, which Go cannot enforce within a package. What the guard buys is that the failure is loud and safe instead of silent and off; it does not buy prevention.

The 'zero bare ink references' invariant that makes the kill-switch safe is a property of DB CONTENT, not of code, and nothing enforces it. A future migration adding a bare var(--color-primary-ink) consumer would make the disabled path drop that declaration entirely. No test can pin this because the consumers do not live in the repo. Recorded at the field with its query; a periodic check would be the real fix and is not built.

I declined reuse_agent's sites.style_overrides suggestion on the grounds that it is a dead column (0/40 populated, no readers). That is a judgement about which kind of debt is worse — reviving a dead column versus adding a config-key convention — and a seat may reasonably weigh it the other way.
